newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian police detained over attack plans.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian police detained over attack plans.

text.p: Palestinian security forces have detained several of their own police officers on Israeli accusations they planned to attack Jewish settlers, officials said on Sunday.

"An investigative committee that formed two days ago is continuing its work to check the allegations against the members of the Palestinian police," the official Palestinian WAFA news agency said on Sunday.
"Some members have been detained to question them about these allegations," it said.
A spokesman for Palestinian President Yasser Arafat confirmed the report.
Israel had accused Palestinian police of carrying out a shooting attack that damaged the car of a rabbi in the West Bank a week and a half ago and planning other attacks on settlers.
They demanded that Palestinian police arrest Deputy Commander Jihad Masouni, a senior official in the Nablus police they said had ordered the attack.
A spokesman for Arafat could not say if Masouni was under arrest nor how many police officers were detained.
Israel arrested three Palestinian police officers last week, saying they were on their way to attack Har Bracha, a Jewish settlement near the Palestinian-ruled city of Nablus in the West Bank.
They also arrested another police officer on suspicion of planning attacks near the West Bank town of Tulkarm.
Palestinians have demanded the Israelis turn over the officers so they can interrogate them.

"The Palestinian police prisoners who are being held by the Israelis should be handed over to the Palestinian Authority for the continuation of the investigation," a spokesman for security forces told WAFA.
Palestinian police operate in parts of the West Bank and the Gaza Strip under Israel-PLO peace deals reached since 1993.

Security cooperation between Israeli and Palestinian troops outlined in the deals has broken down since a March deadlock with the Jewish state over the construction of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
